name: Ketamine
tierNotes: Threshold: slight softness, nothing more (all curves smooth — nothing spikes early).
Light: mild vertical doubling (toned down a notch per feedback) + painting-flattening begins; colors cool.

Common: doubling, frame-hold stutter, desaturation toward gray-blue; by upper-Common, environmental cubism/scenery-slicing has already woken up (moved earlier per user feedback) — the painting starts looking assembled from large, softly-bounded, faintly mismatched glossy panels (PsychonautWiki's own documented ketamine geometry, milder and less intricate than a psychedelic fractal), now with a stable 9-tap wide-average (was 4-tap, which shimmered/aliased against fine texture as the facet breathing slowly drifted the sample point — that's what read as 'jittery/vibrating').

Strong: world visibly shrinking inside a dark surround, the boundary now a true circle (not a rounded rectangle) with a very wide, soft feather and a slow multi-harmonic breathe on its own radius — an irregular blob that continuously swells and settles rather than a fixed geometric cutout; tunnel forming (late vignette wakes); cubism fully readable, including a growing loss of the hard-edge protection that used to keep mortar lines/object outlines fully crisp against the swimming rest of the painting.

Heavy: full k-hole — scene collapses inside that same soft breathing circular boundary (recession pushed further per feedback — the surround now eats significantly more of the frame); doubling and stutter are extreme. Above ~0.7 the receded painting's own structure starts visibly crawling/breathing along its real contours (edge-tangent advection, not a free-floating warp), and above ~0.8 its colour gives way to a continuous, texture/luminance-masked pattern advected along those same contours (rewritten after feedback that the first version's per-facet approach produced a hard 'V' seam and read as an unrelated cloud drifting over the image) — flat, posterized, desaturated-cool and tinted from the photo's own dominant palette, taking inspiration from the psychedelics' structure-driven pattern language while staying in ketamine's own documented 'algorithmic'/low-complexity register, never LSD/DMT's rainbow or fractal tiling. The image is genuinely gone by full Heavy, dissolved into its own breathing pattern rather than covered by one.
